title: Facilitated dissociation of nucleoid-associated proteins from DNA in the bacterial confinement.
authors: Kosar, Zafer; Attar, A Goktug; Erbas, Aykut
one_liner_zh: 该文用粗粒化分子模拟研究细菌核仁相关蛋白（NAP）在染色体受限环境中的DNA解离机制，聚焦蛋白-DNA互作动态与浓度耦合，方法为物理模拟，虽非典型TF-DNA但机制可迁移至转录因子结合研究。
abstract: Transcription machinery depends on the temporal formation of protein-DNA complexes. Recent experiments demonstrated that not only the formation but also the lifetime of such complexes can affect the transcriptional machinery. In parallel, in vitro single-molecule studies showed that nucleoid-associated proteins (NAPs) leave the DNA rapidly as the bulk concentration of the protein increases via facilitated dissociation (FD). Nevertheless, whether such a concentration-dependent mechanism is functional in a bacterial cell, in which NAP levels and the 3d chromosomal structure are often coupled, is not clear a priori. Here, by using extensive coarse-grained molecular simulations, we model the unbinding of specific and nonspecific dimeric NAPs from a high-molecular-weight circular DNA molecule in a cylindrical structure mimicking the cellular confinement of a bacterial chromosome. Our simulations confirm that physiologically relevant peak protein levels (tens of micromolar) lead to highly compact chromosomal structures. This compaction results in rapid off rates (shorter DNA residence times) for specifically DNA-binding NAPs, such as the factor for inversion stimulation, which mostly dissociate via a segmental jump mechanism. Contrarily, for nonspecific NAPs, which are more prone to leave their binding sites via 1d sliding, the off rates decrease as the protein levels increase. The simulations with restrained chromosome models reveal that chromosome compaction is in favor of faster dissociation but only for specific proteins, and nonspecific proteins are not affected by the chromosome compaction. Overall, our results suggest that the cellular concentration level of a structural DNA-binding protein can be highly intermingled with its DNA residence time.
abstract_zh: 转录机制依赖于蛋白质-DNA复合物的时间性形成。近期实验表明，不仅这些复合物的形成，而且其寿命也能影响转录机制。与此同时，体外单分子研究显示，随着蛋白质整体浓度通过促进解离（facilitated dissociation, FD）增加，核仁相关蛋白（nucleoid-associated proteins, NAPs）会迅速离开DNA。然而，这种浓度依赖性机制是否在细菌细胞中发挥作用，其中NAP水平和三维染色体结构常常耦合，尚不明确。在此，通过使用广泛的粗粒化分子模拟，我们模拟了特异性和非特异性二聚体NAPs从高分子量环状DNA分子上解离的过程，该DNA分子处于模拟细菌染色体细胞限制的圆柱形结构中。我们的模拟证实，生理相关的峰值蛋白质水平（数十微摩尔）导致高度紧凑的染色体结构。这种紧凑化导致特异性DNA结合NAPs（如反转刺激因子）的快速解离速率（较短的DNA停留时间），这些蛋白主要通过片段跳跃机制解离。相反，对于更倾向于通过一维滑动离开其结合位点的非特异性NAPs，随着蛋白质水平增加，解离速率降低。使用受限染色体模型的模拟揭示，染色体紧凑化有利于更快解离，但仅对特异性蛋白质有效，而非特异性蛋白质不受染色体紧凑化影响。总体而言，我们的结果表明，结构性DNA结合蛋白的细胞浓度水平可能与其DNA停留时间高度交织。
